title: 1966 AHSME Problem 32
statement: Let \(M\) be the midpoint of side \(AB\) of triangle \(ABC.\) Let \(P\) be a point on \(AB\) between \(A\) and \(M,\) and let \(MD\) be drawn parallel to \(PC\) and intersecting \(BC\) at \(D.\) If the ratio of the area of triangle \(BPD\) to that of triangle \(ABC\) is denoted by \(r,\) then:

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: \(\dfrac12\lt r\lt1\) depending upon the position of \(P\)

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
\(\dfrac12\leq r\lt1\) depending upon the position of
\(P\)

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
\(\dfrac13\lt r\lt\dfrac23\) depending upon the position of
\(P\)

solutions.text:
Since \(MD\parallel PC,\) triangles \(MDP\) and \(MDC\) have the same base \(MD\) and equal altitudes, so their areas are equal. Hence \[ \begin{aligned} [BPD] &=[BMD]+[MDP]\\ &=[BMD]+[MDC]\\ &=[BMC]. \end{aligned} \] Because \(CM\) is a median, \([BMC]=\frac{[ABC]}{2}.\) Thus \(r=\frac{1}{2}\) for every allowed \(P.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Triangles \(MDP\) and \(MDC\) have equal bases on parallel lines
Add their areas to \([BMD]\) and use that \(CM\) is a median
